newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercial demand.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercial demand.

text.p: WCE new crop canola futures ended up on commercial demand, traders said.
"Cargill and UGG sold July and August but commission houses and commercials were buying November," a canola trader said. "Crushers bought November and there was some short covering."
November WCE canola crush profit margins rose to -1.59 Tuesday from -3.70 Monday. Aug-Nov spread from $17.50 to $15.
August canola closed $0.10 higher at $364 per tonne and November settled up $2.30 at $348.60.

September flax lost $0.50 to end at $287.50 on local liquidation and November flax ended $1 lower at $285 as Cargill sold on the close, traders said. About 50 Sep-Nov flax spread at $2, 5 July-Sep $41.
October western barley rose $2.70 to settle at $128.70 on commercial buying and December closed up $2.40 at $129.50. Volume was 1,075 lots.

October feed wheat rose $1.80 to end at $152.70 and December closed up $1.40 at $153.20 as commercials and LFG bought from locals, floor sources said. July-Oct spread at $3.50, Oct-Dec $1. Volume was 889 lots.
UGG and RBC-DS bought 75 December oats contracts up US$1.50 to US$114. Feed peas did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except oats, feed peas in U.S. dollars.)
